topics.label: Course Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening framing introduces the lecturer, sets the lecture in the context of the series, and outlines the session's learning outcomes.

topics.label: Etiology of Cancer: Intrinsic Mutagenesis Versus Environmental Exposures
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the foundational causes of cancer, contrasting intrinsic biological mutagenesis and bad luck with extrinsic environmental risk factors supported by epidemiological evidence.

topics.label: Pathogen-Driven Oncogenesis and Burkitt Lymphoma
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious pathogens drive oncogenesis, using Burkitt lymphoma as a detailed mechanistic case study.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Mutagenesis by Chemical and Physical Carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how physical radiation and chemical agents induce DNA damage directly or through endogenous metabolic activation and oxidative stress.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion and the Multi-Stage Model of Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the concept of tumor promotion, illustrating how non-mutagenic stimuli such as chronic inflammation and aberrant signaling drive the expansion of initiated cells.

topics.label: Host Susceptibility Factors and Carcinogenesis Summary
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address how host developmental stages and tissue contexts modulate cancer risk, providing a synthesis of carcinogenic mechanisms.

topics.label: Methodologies for Identifying and Assessing Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the genomic, epidemiological, animal, and in vitro methodologies used to detect and establish the carcinogenicity of various agents.

topics.label: Lecture Summary and Risk-Benefit Framing
topics.groupedBecause: This closing framing concludes the lecture with a summary of environmental cancer risks and a perspective on everyday risk-benefit decision-making.
